value.rationale: Strict dephasing on half of an otherwise fully connected positive-hopping ring generically destroys all initial-state memory, but a codimension-one parity-constrained product resonance retains it. The theorem characterizes the complete memory map for any initial state and gives an even-size family retaining a positive local return while an arbitrarily small generic bond detuning restores fully mixed behavior. This motivates exact comparison of decoherence-free modes with global mixing, beyond trivial finite-size kernel counting.
